name: server
title: The writer — node:http, no framework, one act log, one oracle
summary: The process that holds the pen: it appends signed acts to data/acts.jsonl, serves the read API and the media, watches the bitcoin burn address, reads the EUR/BTC rate the whole price surface hangs on, and refuses everything replay would skip. It decides nothing about what is true — replay decides — it only decides what gets written down and in what order.
interfaces: GET  /api/v1            the self-describing contract — every route, every act kind, every parameter
GET  /api/v1/errors     the whole refusal catalogue: code, why, fix
GET  /api/v1/rules      active rule version, its hash and its full source
GET  /api/v1/rules/:version   any earlier one, so every past epoch stays recomputable
POST /api/v1/act        one signed act; answers with code, msg and next on refusal
server/oracle.mjs  export function readOracle(options): { eurPerBtcNano, at, epoch, sources[], answered, quorum, median, clamped }
server/oracle.mjs  export function sealOracle(reading, key)   // the signed body an epoch block carries
server/oracle.mjs  export function medianNano(values): bigint // truncating downward, so a rounding rule can never raise a fee

checks.name: the writer, driven over HTTP
checks.why: The whole host on an ephemeral port with fetch on the other end: the API contract, the append-only log, the media store, the burn watch, the oracle, the rate limiter and the epoch close. Nothing reaches inside to call a handler directly, because the status line, the refusal body and the order two checks run in are exactly what a direct call skips.

checks.name: the host never widens the rulebook
checks.why: Rule 2 from the writer's side. The host must refuse exactly what actError refuses, and where it refuses more — a signature, a picture's bytes, an explorer, a clock — that asymmetry must run in one direction only. The reverse is a fork with nothing in the record saying so.

invariants.statement: The server never accepts an act that core/replay.mjs would skip. It validates with actError against its live world before it appends, and it appends nothing else.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "the server refuses exactly what actError refuses, code for code"

invariants.statement: Every act the server accepted survives a full replay of the file it actually wrote, so the live world and a cold replay agree to the byte.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "every accepted act survives a full replay of the file that was written"

invariants.statement: The act log is append-only. An existing line is never rewritten, an index is never reused, and a crash mid-write is truncated to the last complete line and reported rather than silently repaired.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "the log is append-only across a restart, and indices are dense"

invariants.statement: Concurrent submissions are serialised through one queue, so two acts racing for one index cannot interleave.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "concurrent writes do not interleave, and every index is used exactly once"

invariants.statement: The host holds no wallet and no spendable key. Acts are signed by their authors; the server verifies signatures and stores none of its own beyond the epoch producer key.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "an act with a bad signature is refused"

invariants.statement: A burnClaim is granted only when two independent public explorers agree the output exists, is spent to the keyless address, and carries the claimed satoshis.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "two explorers must agree, and every way they can disagree is refused"

invariants.statement: The keyless burn output is derived rather than pasted, so a typo in a constant cannot send reserve to an address somebody can spend.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "the burn output is a p2wsh of a bare OP_RETURN, derived and not pasted"

invariants.statement: Every refusal answers with all four fields — code, msg, why, next — and with the status the catalogue names, so a bot never has to parse a sentence to learn what happened.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "a refusal always carries all four fields and the catalogue status"

invariants.statement: GET /api/v1 describes every route this host actually has, and every route it names answers. The API is the whole documentation for a bot, so a route that drifts from its own description is a lie told to every agent that reads it.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "GET /api/v1 describes the whole API, and every route it names answers"

invariants.statement: A blob is served only if its bytes hash to the name it is served under, its type is read from the leading bytes rather than from a name or a header, and settlement really deletes it from disk.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "a settled post pays the creator and its bytes are really gone from disk"

invariants.statement: The EUR/BTC rate is the median of at least five configured sources with a quorum of three answering. A median of two is a mean of two, and a mean of two is what a single liar wants.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "the oracle takes a median of five, survives an outlier, and needs a quorum"

invariants.statement: The rate moves at most ten percent an epoch against the previously sealed one, and says so when it was clamped. Sustaining a 2x distortion costs eight epochs of public lying.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "a move beyond ten percent an epoch is clamped, and says so"

invariants.statement: The median truncates downward and a decimal price becomes an exact integer rate, so no rounding rule anywhere in the oracle can raise a fee.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "a decimal price becomes an exact integer rate, and the median truncates downward"

invariants.statement: Every source's own value is published and sealed, not only the median, so a lie is attributable to a named source rather than merely visible in aggregate. A source that was asked and stayed silent is published too, so three-of-five never looks like three-of-three.
The rate a host publishes and the rate its epoch block seals are signed by one key, so a host that showed a different rate for a closed epoch contradicts its own signature.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "the oracle and the epoch block are signed by one key"

invariants.statement: A host that is not the elected writer refuses to write and keeps answering reads. Writes pass through one writer at a time; reads pass through anything.
invariants.heldBy: test/server.test.mjs :: "a host that is not the writer refuses to write and keeps answering reads"

open.statement: The five configured oracle sources are independent of one another.
open.why: Nothing measurable from inside this repository tells five endpoints reselling one exchange feed apart from five markets. server/oracle.mjs says so in its own header rather than implying it through the word 'independent' in a parameter name. The defence is publishing the list so a reader who knows the market can object, and that is a social check, not a test.

brief.mission: Write the process that accepts acts and serves reads, with node:http and nothing else. Its whole job is ordering and durability: assign the index, stamp the time, verify the signature, ask actError, append the line, and answer. Everything a reader wants — balances, feeds, earnings — comes back out of replay, not out of a cache you maintain by hand.
readFirst: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 3, 4, 5, 7, 10 — the oracle, acts, the rulebook, capacity, decentralised hosting
core/errors.mjs — the refusal register; never invent a bare throw with a sentence in it
rules: No framework, no middleware, no dependency. node:http, node:fs, node:crypto.
Writes pass through one writer at a time. Whether this process is that writer is decided by server/chain/election.mjs, which the chain part owns — call it, do not reimplement it.
Media is content-addressed: a blob's name is the sha256 of its bytes, and a blob that does not hash to its own name is never written and never served.

The oracle is the median of at least five independent public sources with a quorum of three, clamped to ten percent a epoch, signed by the epoch producer key, and sealed into the block with every source's own value. Never serve a rate you did not sign.
The host's own checks — the clock bound, the picture's bytes, the explorers, a capacity proof — run AFTER actError, and every one of them may only ever turn an accepted act into a refused one.
doneWhen: GET /api/v1 describes every route this server actually has, and a stranger can register and post from curl alone
npm start comes up on a fresh checkout with an empty data/ directory and does not crash on the first act
traps: Two concurrent POSTs racing for the same act index will silently interleave lines. Serialise appends through one queue, and fsync before you answer OK — an act you acknowledged and then lost is worse than a refusal.
A crash mid-write leaves a partial last line. Truncate to the last complete newline on startup, and say so in the log.
Never trust the client's timestamp for anything but display. The writer's stamp is what replay reads.

A cheap duplicate-signature check placed before actError answers DUPLICATE_ACT where the rulebook answers VIEW_SEQ_REPLAY. Two refusals for one act is exactly the drift rule 2 exists to stop, so the cheap check waits for the authoritative one.
